predecessors.name: Mataram Sultanate
predecessors.text: Madura, from which the rebel army crossed, and the northern coastal towns of Mataram

successors.name: Mataram Sultanate
successors.text: Kediri, the rebels' last base, which fell on 25 November 1678

ledger.x: September 1676 (no month stored, so that the undated coast sweep can follow in order): Trunajaya's army crosses from Madura and routs the royal force at Gegodog.

1676-1677: the rebels take the Java north coast. the page has rebels take most northern coastal towns, from Surabaya to Cirebon, except Jepara; the lord of Giri had joined the rebellion in early 1676.
1677: Madura and the remaining coast towns pass out of rebel hands.
April 1677: a VOC fleet under Cornelis Speelman takes Surabaya.
1677, entered at 1678: the rebels lose Plered to Pangeran Puger.
25 November 1678: Kediri falls to VOC and Mataram forces under François Tack. the page has Kediri fall on 25 November 1678, after the three-column march of September-November.
November 1678: the rebel state is crushed.

wars.name: Trunajaya rebellion
wars.outcome: The VOC and Mataram crushed the rebels; Kediri fell on 25 November 1678, Trunajaya surrendered on 26 December 1679, the lord of Giri was beaten in April 1680 and Puger was pardoned in November 1681.

certainty.note: The page names towns, not boundaries; every region is a radius round a town or a chain of circles on Madura.
